summary: Dire Bear Form the whole fight: Mangle (Bear) on cooldown (top threat), Lacerate to build and hold a 5-stack bleed, Maul as the off-GCD rage dump, Swipe for AoE. Maintain Faerie Fire (Feral) and Demoralizing Roar. Bears have no block/parry - mitigation is passive armor + dodge, so there's no per-GCD defensive cast.

Shred.note: Cat Form ability - the druid is in Cat (DPS), not Bear; no tanking armor or threat

Rip.note: Cat Form finisher - wrong form for tanking

Mangle (Cat).note: Cat Form ability - tank should be in Bear Form using Mangle (Bear)

Ferocious Bite.note: Cat Form finisher - wrong form for tanking

Rake.note: Cat Form bleed - wrong form for tanking

Survival Instincts.note: does NOT exist in TBC Classic (WotLK ability) - log is mislabeled or wrong-expansion

Berserk.note: does NOT exist in TBC Classic (WotLK ability)

Healing Touch.note: caster-form heal - a tank shapeshifting out to heal loses all mitigation; emergency only

breakpoint.note: Mangle (Bear) cast count should be near its theoretical max (used on its ~6s cooldown) - it's the top single-target threat and the #1 bear competence signal. Lacerate should ramp to and hold a 5-stack bleed. Maul (off the GCD) should appear frequently as the rage dump, riding alongside Mangle/Lacerate; no Maul means rage capping and wasted threat.

advisory: TBC bear tank. Should be in Dire Bear Form the entire fight - any Cat-form abilities (Shred, Rip, Rake, Mangle Cat) mean the druid is in Cat (DPS), not tanking. Bears have no Shield Block/Holy Shield equivalent; mitigation is passive (high armor + dodge), so don't expect a per-GCD defensive cast. Frenzied Regeneration is a cooldown-style self-heal on damage spikes (a handful per fight), not a rotational ability. Barkskin and Challenging Roar (AoE taunt) are situational cooldowns. Survival Instincts and Berserk do NOT exist in TBC.
